author.heading: About Erich Fromm
author.bio: Erich Fromm (1900–1980) was a German-American social psychologist and psychoanalyst associated with the Frankfurt School. A refugee from Nazi Germany, he helped found the William Alanson White Institute in New York; his books connect individual character with the pressures of social life.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In the chapter on the theory of love, Fromm describes a child’s movement from receiving care toward developing the capacity to give it. The paired formulations distinguish dependence on another person from an active capacity to love; they are part of that developmental argument, rather than advice to deny all human needs.
